YOUR CURVES & GLUTE GOAL

Grow strength. Support your shape.

Build your glutes

Use controlled hip-extension, hip-abduction, bridge and squat patterns. Start with manageable practice and recovery between demanding days. Gradually increase the challenge as your current movements become easier.

Train your core and whole body

Core work supports control and strength. It does not selectively burn belly fat. Waist appearance also depends on overall body composition, genetics and other factors; no routine guarantees a flat stomach or a particular silhouette.

Fuel your training

Eat varied meals with enough food and protein, and protect sleep and recovery. This goal does not automatically prescribe weight loss or a restrictive diet. Bodyweight practice is a starting point; ongoing muscle growth may need greater resistance.

Track your own progress

Record comfortable glute-practice repetitions using the same movement and method. Waist and hip measurements are optional and can change for several reasons. Neither a tape measurement nor a repetition result is a “Figure 8” score.

YOUR SCHEDULE

A week at a time.

Rest days are part of your plan. Your actual completed sessions remain in your journal.

Fuel your routine.

Choose varied food and regular hydration. Weight tracking is optional; no calorie prescriptions or extreme diets are provided.

Recovery counts.

Protect sleep and rest between demanding sessions. More soreness does not mean better progress.

Measure what matters.

Track activity, consistency or a comfortable performance assessment. Your chosen target is a direction, not a guaranteed result.

Guidance and important context +

For ages 16 and above. Teen plans exclude weight-loss targets and maximal-effort testing. Choose your ability, not a gender label. Consult a qualified professional if you have a medical condition, injury, recent surgery, pregnancy or postpartum recovery.

Stop and seek urgent help for chest pain, fainting or severe breathing difficulty. Generic performance goals are independent of armed forces and do not provide official test scores.
